title: Groundnut Soup with Sweet Potato and Kale
summary: Sweet potato simmers in coconut milk with ginger, garlic, chilli and turmeric, then pounded peanuts turn it thick and creamy. Kale and a squeeze of lime finish a filling, warming bowl that happens to be plant-based.
equipment: large casserole or heavy pot (about 5 litres) with a lid
pestle and mortar or food processor

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped
fresh coriander, stems finely chopped and leaves picked
green chilli, finely chopped (seeds in for more heat)
spring onions, whites chopped, greens thinly sliced for serving
sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks

ingredients.note: 30 g kept back, chopped, for serving

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
curly kale, tough stems removed, leaves torn into bite-size pieces
lime juice, plus wedges to serve

steps.title: Soften the aromatics
steps.text: Heat the oil in the casserole over medium heat and add the garlic, ginger, coriander stems, chilli and spring-onion whites. Cook, stirring, for 2-3 minutes until soft and fragrant but not browned, then stir in the turmeric, tomato purée and cayenne for 1 minute. A minute in the hot oil cooks out the raw edge of the tomato purée and blooms the spices.

steps.title: Simmer the sweet potato
steps.text: Pour in the coconut milk, stock and water, add the sweet potato and bring to the boil. Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, until a piece crushes easily against the side of the pot. Fully tender sweet potato blends into the base and helps thicken it.

steps.title: Pound the peanuts
steps.text: While the soup simmers, chop 30 g of the peanuts for the topping. Pound or blend the rest to a coarse, sandy paste. A slightly rough texture gives body without turning the soup into peanut butter.

steps.title: Thicken the soup
steps.text: Whisk the peanut paste and salt into the soup, then blend about a third of it with the stick blender so it turns creamy but still has some chunks. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, stirring often. Peanuts sink and catch easily, so keep the spoon moving across the base.

steps.title: Add the greens
steps.text: Stir in the kale and simmer for 3-5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Take the pot off the heat, add the lime juice and loosen with a splash of water if it is very thick. The lime cuts through the richness of the coconut and peanuts.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Ladle into bowls and scatter with the chopped peanuts, coriander leaves and spring-onion greens. Serve with lime wedges for squeezing. The fresh herbs and crunchy nuts add contrast to the smooth soup.

tips: Use unsalted roasted peanuts; salted ones make the soup far too salty.
A common mistake is walking away once the peanuts go in: the soup sticks quickly, so stir and keep the heat gentle.
The soup thickens as it stands; thin it with a little water when reheating.
For more heat, leave the seeds in the chilli or add an extra pinch of cayenne.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months (the kale softens further on freezing). Reheat gently, stirring and adding water, until piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
